newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Prices slip on sell pressure.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Prices slip on sell pressure.

text.p: Singapore gas oil and jet fuel slipped on Tuesday following a deluge of offers but a free fall was prevented by the buying support by some traders at a lower level, industry sources said.

Three 150,000-barrel gas oil cargoes traded, two at $25.30 per barrel, free-on-board Singapore, was sold by a European major and a Swiss trader to a local trader for loading on May 21-25 and June 1-5, traders said.

One trader said the bid by the local trader at $25.30 per barrel for cargoes lifting in mid-May and early June gives an impression of a flat physical market despite the more than 60 cent backwardation on the May/June swaps market, one trader said.

But another 150,000-barrel for June 1-5 loading traded at at $25.15 per barrel was more in line with the backwardated market, traders said. The cargo was sold by a European major to a Chinese bunker trader with storage facilities in Malaysia.
On Monday, one cargo traded at $25.30, traders said.
Traders said about seven offers were heard with some sellers offering two cargoes for loading within the May 24 to June 5 period.
The lower prices did not surprise many but most were amazed by the sustained buying power of a group of traders.
Two local traders and one Japanese trader have since March 3 bought nearly 19 million barrels of gas oil and there were speculations that the traders may wind down their purchases in May.
Reflective of the buying mood of these traders, the swaps market was last quoted steady from Monday at $25.10/$25.20 per barrel, brokers said.
"There is alot of support for the market at the $25.00 mark," one broker said.

Jet fuel also slipped slightly with a 100,000-barrel cargo loading on May 21-25 traded at $25.00 per barrel between a U.S. major and a local trader compared to the $25.10 and $25.30 buying number on Monday.
Bangladesh Petroleum Corp has deferred the closing date for its tender to buy superior kerosene by one day to May 7 with offers valid to May 15.
The tender seeks 155,000-barrels of kerosene for May 23-24 delivery on a cost-and- freight (c-and-f) basis to Chittagong.
